extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and screenwriters revising dialogue
extracted.subtask_description: A revision-focused technique for placing a character's most important word or phrase at the end of their line so the next speaker responds to that pivot, producing clearer, snappier, and forward-moving dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-position core word/phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The last word or phrase of each speech is the core word that seals meaning and cues a reaction from the other side of the scene.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the most important phrase at the end of a character's line so it functions as the conversational cue the next speaker reacts to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position cue to prompt direct response
rubrics_metrics.description: Position the most important phrase at the end of a character's line, prompting the next speaker to respond directly to that element rather than earlier content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates natural rhythm and forward momentum; revise lines so responses latch onto the end-weighted cue rather than diffuse earlier material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use diagnostic revision questions
rubrics_metrics.description: As a revision tool, ask: (1) What cue is Character B responding to in Character A's dialogue? (2) Where is that cue located?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the answer shows B responding to non-pivotal or buried material, relocate or rewrite lines so the cue is clear and appropriately positioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: In long speeches, make the final pivot explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: For longer speeches, characters don't respond to bulk philosophical content or backstory; they pick up the final question or directive — the conversational pivot point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the pivot (question/directive) appears at the end of the speech so partners can plausibly and directly respond; avoid expecting other characters to engage with long internal exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting disconnection by internal cues
rubrics_metrics.description: For disconnected dialogue, characters can respond to their own internal cues rather than their partner's, effectively depicting when people don't listen to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally have a character's response track an internal word/phrase or thought rather than the partner's last cue to show miscommunication or inattention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired effect: clarity, snappiness, and forward movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes dialogue 'easy to follow, keeps it snappy, and ideally allows the movement of the dialogue to be easily understood.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use end-weighted cues and the above revision checks to achieve these goals—clear beats, rhythmic exchanges, and visible conversational momentum.
